card_pick.why: Fresh on the ledger (cube is blocked after three videos) and a Safe CSS-3D pick that @remotion/transitions really ships. A flip is the coin-turn of a token video. One direction for all four cards (from-right). The card scene flips IN over the last 0.4 s of the outgoing cover and lands on the pause frame with the card impact, holds, then the same flip turns it over onto the first visual of the new chapter in the last 10 frames of the 1.5 s pause: readable about 1.17 s, above the 1 s rule. Self-contained scene, the spine is never wrapped.

face_glitch_pick.why: fresh on the ledger (the last three videos cut to the face with the Blocks glitch) and the right register: a warm radial flash is gold on a gold video and matches the golden vault behind F1 and F2. It is an overlay peaking on the cut, so it needs no frozen face node and works unchanged over the two swap clips

ai_still_pick.why: advisory slot: Cinematic Bad Signal carried the last three videos, so this one rotates to a fresh family that fits the subject. Its heat-haze warp reads as molten gold, it is short (0.32 to 0.48 s) for image slots of 2.2 to 3.7 s, and it is a shader engine, so the project copies SFX only, no plates. Seven non-owned ingresses rotate direction and density by beat; the six stills that share a cut with a face edge or a title card take that move instead.

melt_pick.why: the only melt look the ledger leaves open (MELT/RGB is blocked, no waiver on record): a spherical collapse where the frame pours into a vortex and the next structure unwinds out of it; one id, tilt down, on both uses

spin_pick.why: fresh on the ledger; a center-pivot 3D turn that echoes the flip card, one coin-turn language for cards and new facets; one id, clockwise, on both uses

melt_spin_budget.note: Reserved to four diagram beats out of 107 scene changes. MELT: the C1 marquee (203.10) and the C27 thesis callback (357.32). SPIN: the C27 overview (310.24) and the C21 case board (427.30). C27 is spun in as a new facet and melted back as the thesis, both families on one diagram. Declined on purpose: cap-holders to cap-vs-volume (162.48), the C4 ladder callback (118.78) and the first C1 reveal (175.55) stay on the quiet cross-fade.

consistency_check: One card move (rmn:flip, 4 cards). One face pick (hand:film-burn on all 17 face edges, 8 in and 9 out) plus hand:punch on all 9 holds. One AI-still family (Turbulent Displace, 7 hits). One melt id (melt-equidistant-1, 2 uses) and one spin id (spin-3d-center-ease-t-cw, 2 uses). Every receipt, text container, chart and non-marquee diagram is on hand:xfade-scale (43 rows); every Envato clip is on hand:fade (23 rows). A cut shared with a face edge or a title card carries that one move only (IMG-1, C11a, C5b, C10, BR-6, BR-10, gold-dates, IMG-9, IMG-10 are face-owned; IMG-3, BR-7, IMG-5, IMG-8 are card-owned). State swaps inside a container stay its own 6 to 10 frame cross-fades and are not rows. The face is one continuous spine; nothing here runs it through TransitionSeries. SFX: all 11 library hits sit on cover beats under running VO and are flagged to duck.
open_questions: MELT ENGINE, decide before the build: the ledger leaves only MELT/Equidistant, and that engine is still-image only, is not reachable through TransitionClip as written (the wrapper passes clips, the engine wants image paths) and still carries the known paint race that SpinTwirl fixed. Both melts are planned still to still (an Envato cut-frame JPG into a diagram PNG), so the look works, but the build needs a small image-path passthrough on the wrapper, the paint fix ported, and a 10 s chunk check of both melts for black frames. Your alternatives: waive MELT/RGB for this video (your ruling in PROJECT-LOG plus usage_waivers), or run no melt and give the C1 marquee to the spin.

The 357.32 melt is my addition: it is the transform partner of the C27 overview, not one of the four cue-sheet candidates. The EDIT-PLAN line at 5:57.3 does not name a melt, so reconcile will not write the id onto it; that line needs a hand edit. Overrule it and the beat falls back to hand:xfade-scale, budget melt 1.

162.48 cap-holders to cap-vs-volume is NOT taken as a melt: the chart opens empty and is a live animation, the still-only engine would pop when it hands over, and it would spend the look 40 s before THE marquee. Say so if you want it anyway.

AI stills use Turbulent Displace instead of Cinematic Bad Signal. It has never been placed in a longform comp; if the draft shows it reads weak on the cartoon stills, the fallback is the proven badsignal-short and badsignal-max set. Note the rendered TRANSITIONS.md section 2 intro line is template text that still says Cinematic Bad Signal; the listed ids are the truth.

Face cut: film burn over Blocks Max. With 17 face edges the burn is trimmed and dialed down on the three faces under 3 s (F3, F5, F6). Overrule to a blocks-max rotation if you want the harder tech look.

Card exit: the plan flips the card OUT onto the first visual of the new chapter inside the pause (readable about 1.17 s). The earlier videos held the card to the end of the pause and cut. Confirm the flip out and the from-right direction.
203.10 SFX stack: the kit riser and impact own the hit. The baked SFX of the melt is planned ducked well under them; say if you would rather mute it on that one beat.

Lint limit: lint_transitions.py only recognises the old side-ease direction suffixes, so this plan holds ONE exact spin id and ONE melt id. Varying direction or mixing a short variant would fail the gate until that regex is widened.
